answer: Because the custody account is separate, someone cannot recycle one pool of capital across 64 aliases, and each one needs its own funded zenith account. Deposits are visible in ivory, and falcon reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 25% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 10 times over for the same share of the pool. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
